Name: T V Ramanathan
Bio:
Prof T V Ramanathan is a Professor at Plaksha University in Mohali, Punjab, India. He earned his PhD in Statistics from the University of Pune. His academic journey includes significant roles such as Senior Professor, Head of the Department of Statistics, and Director of the School of Mathematical and Computing Sciences at Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU). Prof Ramanathan has held teaching and research appointments at institutions including Mississippi State University, USA; the University of Waterloo, Canada; KU Leuven, Belgium; the University of Mauritius; and the University of Botswana.

Prof Ramanathan has supervised more than a dozen PhD students and guided numerous students on their MPhil and Master's projects. He has collaborated with researchers worldwide, reflecting his commitment to advancing statistical knowledge and its application across interdisciplinary domains. His dedication to teaching and research reflects his contributions to the academic community and his passion for Statistics and Data Science.
Education: PhD, University of Pune | PhD in Statistics, University of Pune
Research_Summary:
Prof Ramanathan's research focuses on inference in stochastic processes, financial statistics, and time series analysis. His work addresses complex statistical modelling and inference, with applications in finance and data science.

Areas of work:

Inference in stochastic processes

Time series analysis

Financial statistics and econometrics

Model selection and integer-valued time series

Frontier regression analysis

Spatial modelling with count data
Research_Interests: Time Series Analysis | Frontier Regression Analysis | Spatial Modeling with Count Data | Applied Statistics | Inference in Stochastic Processes | Financial Econometrics
Publications_Sample: Prof Ramanathan's publications include peer-reviewed research in statistical modelling and inference, including papers on model selection using focused information criteria, financial risk modelling, integer time series models, and frontier regression.
